# classmcp — complete setup and operations guide for AI agents

> classmcp is a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives a coding
> agent read access to a student's Google Classroom account (courses, due and
> missing work, assignments, materials, announcements, Drive attachments) and
> best-effort submission. It runs on the user's own computer over stdio, uses
> the user's own Google OAuth Desktop credentials, and has no hosted backend
> and no telemetry.

This file is written for agents (Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, and any
other MCP host). It is self-contained: you should not need the README to set
classmcp up. If something here conflicts with the README, the README in the
repository is the source of truth; report the conflict to the user.

## Facts you need

- Repository: https://github.com/khurrambhutto/classmcp
- Issues: https://github.com/khurrambhutto/classmcp/issues
- npm package: `gcrclassmcp` (https://www.npmjs.com/package/gcrclassmcp)
- Command: `classmcp` (the package name and the command name differ)
- Current version: 0.3.0-rc.1, published on npm under both `latest` and `next`
- Requires: Node.js 20 or newer, a Google account with Google Classroom access
- Transport: stdio. Start command: `classmcp serve`
- License: MIT. Not affiliated with Google.
- Website: https://khurrambhutto.github.io/classmcp/
- Short index for agents: https://khurrambhutto.github.io/classmcp/llms.txt
- This file: https://khurrambhutto.github.io/classmcp/llms-full.txt

CLI subcommands:

```
classmcp serve        Run the MCP server over stdio (used by MCP hosts)
classmcp setup        Store Google OAuth credentials and authorize once (interactive)
classmcp doctor       Diagnose configuration without printing secrets
classmcp --version
classmcp --help
```

## Rules for the agent (read before doing anything)

1. Never ask the user to paste a client secret, OAuth token, or the contents of
   `~/.classmcp/credentials.json` / `tokens.json` into chat. Never print them.
   Never `cat` those files.
2. Never create Google Cloud credentials on the user's behalf. The user does the
   Google Cloud Console steps in their own browser; you explain them.
3. `classmcp setup` is interactive (it reads stdin and opens a browser for
   Google consent). If your shell cannot pass input through to the user, ask
   the user to run `classmcp setup` in their own terminal and tell you when it
   finishes. Do not try to fake or pipe answers into it.
4. Never register a temporary `npx` cache path as the server command. Use the
   global `classmcp` executable or absolute paths (see "Absolute paths").
5. When you edit a host config file, merge: keep every existing server entry,
   setting, and comment. Read the file first. Make a backup copy if the file is
   large or you are unsure.
6. Do not skip verification. If a step fails, stop, report the exact error,
   and say what the user should do. Do not invent output or claim success.
7. `submit_work` with `turnIn: true` turns work in for a real student. Only call
   it when the user explicitly asks, and pass `confirmTurnIn: "I confirm turn in"`
   only after the user confirms.

## Identify your host first

Work out which MCP host you are running inside before registering anything.
Then follow exactly one of these sections:

- You are **Codex** (OpenAI Codex CLI / IDE extension) → "Host: Codex"
- You are **OpenCode** → "Host: OpenCode"
- You are **Claude Code** (CLI, desktop, IDE extension) → "Host: Claude Code"
- You are **anything else** (Cursor, Antigravity, Windsurf, VS Code Copilot,
  Gemini CLI, Zed, Cline, Continue, Goose, a custom client, …) →
  "Host: any other agent". You MUST read your own host's current MCP
  documentation before you register the server. Config file locations and key
  names differ between hosts and change between versions; do not guess.

If you cannot tell which host you are, ask the user.

## Agent setup procedure

Follow these steps in order. Report progress to the user after each step.

### Step 1 — Check the environment

```bash
node --version          # must be v20 or newer
npm --version
classmcp --version      # may fail if not installed yet; that is fine
```

If Node is missing or older than 20, stop and tell the user to install Node 20+
(for example from https://nodejs.org, or with their version manager). If
`classmcp --version` already prints a version, skip Step 2.

### Step 2 — Install

```bash
npm install --global gcrclassmcp@next
classmcp --version
```

If the global install fails with EACCES on macOS/Linux, do not use `sudo`
without asking; suggest a Node version manager or an npm prefix the user owns.

From source (only if the user asks):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/khurrambhutto/classmcp.git
cd classmcp
npm ci
npm install --global .
classmcp --version
```

### Step 3 — Google Cloud credentials (the user does this in a browser)

Explain these steps to the user and wait until they say they are done:

1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/ and create a project (or pick one).
2. Enable the **Google Classroom API** and the **Google Drive API** for that
   project (APIs & Services → Library).
3. Configure the OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform → Branding /
   Audience). Personal Gmail account: choose **External**. Eligible Google
   Workspace account: **Internal** is allowed. If the app's publishing status
   is **Testing**, add the user's own Google account under **Test users**.
4. Create credentials → **OAuth client ID** → application type **Desktop app**.
5. Download the client JSON into the user's `Downloads` folder. Keep the
   default `client_secret_….json` name. `classmcp setup` looks for a file named
   `client_secret*.json` or `credentials*.json` in `~/Downloads`.

School-managed accounts: the school's Workspace admin may block third-party
apps or Classroom API access. If consent is refused with an admin-policy
message, the user must use a different account or ask their admin.

### Step 4 — Authorize

The user runs (or you run, if your terminal is interactive):

```bash
classmcp setup
```

What setup does, in order:

1. Repairs permissions of existing secret files.
2. Finds `client_secret*.json` / `credentials*.json` in `~/Downloads`, or asks
   for the path.
3. Validates it is a Desktop app client and stores it at
   `~/.classmcp/credentials.json` (mode 0600).
4. Opens Google's consent page in the browser (loopback redirect, 5-minute
   timeout). The user approves.
5. Stores tokens in the OS keychain (or `~/.classmcp/tokens.json`, 0600, when
   no keychain is available).
6. Calls Classroom and prints the course list.
7. For each detected host config it asks `Configure <Host> at <file>? [y/N]`.
   Answering `y` writes an entry using absolute Node + script paths for
   Claude Code (`~/.claude.json`), Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`), OpenCode
   (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`, only if the file has no comments) and
   Antigravity (`~/.config/antigravity/mcp.json`). For Codex it only prints the
   command to run and does not modify `config.toml`.

It is fine for the user to answer `N` to every host prompt and let you
register the server in Step 6. If they answered `y`, verify instead of adding
a duplicate entry.

### Step 5 — Diagnose

```bash
classmcp doctor
```

Expected lines start with `ok`, `warn`, or `fail`. Exit code 1 means at least
one `fail`. Secrets are never printed. Fix every `fail` using the
"Troubleshooting" table before continuing. A healthy run ends with
`All checks passed.`

### Step 6 — Register the server with your host

Use the section for your host below. All hosts run the same thing:
command `classmcp`, argument `serve`, transport stdio.

### Step 7 — Reload and verify

1. Restart or reconnect the host so it starts the server.
2. Confirm the host lists exactly these five tools: `get_overview`,
   `get_assignment`, `search`, `download_files`, `submit_work`.
3. Call `get_overview` with `{ "view": "courses" }`. Success = a JSON result
   with a `courses` list. An empty list is a valid result for an account with
   no courses; report it, do not treat it as failure.
4. Tell the user the first thing to try: "What's due this week in my Google
   Classroom courses?" (calls `get_overview` with the default `view: "due"`).
5. Tell the user that submissions are best effort: Google usually blocks
   third-party apps from attaching files to or turning in teacher-created
   assignments, so they may need to finish turn-in in Classroom using the link
   classmcp returns.

## Host: Codex

Official docs: https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp

Register (preferred):

```bash
codex mcp add classmcp -- classmcp serve
codex mcp list
```

Or edit `~/.codex/config.toml` (merge, keep other tables):

```toml
[mcp_servers.classmcp]
command = "classmcp"
args = ["serve"]
startup_timeout_sec = 30
tool_timeout_sec = 300
```

Optional extra working folder for uploads/downloads:

```toml
[mcp_servers.classmcp.env]
CLASSMCP_WORKDIR = "/absolute/path/to/folder"
```

Codex-specific instructions:

- `startup_timeout_sec = 30` and `tool_timeout_sec = 300` are recommended:
  downloads and large scans can take longer than Codex's defaults.
- After registering, start a new Codex session (or restart the IDE extension).
  `codex mcp list` must show `classmcp`.
- If `codex mcp list` shows it but the tools fail to start, replace
  `command`/`args` with absolute paths (see "Absolute paths").

## Host: OpenCode

Official docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/

OpenCode uses the key `mcp` (NOT `mcpServers`). Global config:
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (or `opencode.json`). Project config:
`opencode.json` in the project root. Add under `mcp`, keeping comments and
other entries:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "classmcp": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["classmcp", "serve"],
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 60000
    }
  }
}
```

Optional working folder: add `"environment": { "CLASSMCP_WORKDIR": "/absolute/path" }`
inside the `classmcp` object.

OpenCode-specific instructions:

- `command` is an array (command and arguments together). `type` must be
  `"local"`. `timeout` is in milliseconds; keep 60000.
- If both `opencode.json` and `opencode.jsonc` exist in `~/.config/opencode/`,
  check which one the user actually uses; remove a stale entry that uses an
  old `mcpServers` key or an `npx classmcp@…` command.
- OpenCode often runs without your interactive shell's PATH (version managers
  such as mise, nvm, fnm, asdf, volta). If it reports classmcp as failed or
  timed out, use absolute paths:
  `"command": ["/abs/path/to/node", "/abs/path/to/gcrclassmcp/dist/cli.js", "serve"]`.
- Verify with:

  ```bash
  opencode mcp list
  ```

  Expected: `classmcp connected`.
- If your OpenCode setup calls MCP tools from an `execute` code runtime, use
  bracket notation: `await tools.classmcp["get_overview"]({ view: "courses" })`.
  Dot notation (`tools.classmcp.get_overview`) fails with "unknown tool".

## Host: Claude Code

Official docs: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp

Register for all projects (user scope):

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user classmcp -- classmcp serve
claude mcp list
claude mcp get classmcp
```

Without `--scope user`, Claude Code registers the server only for the current
project directory (local scope). Use `--scope project` only if the user wants
it written to a shared `.mcp.json` in the repository.

Equivalent manual entry (top-level `mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "classmcp": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "classmcp",
      "args": ["serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code-specific instructions:

- Prefer the `claude mcp add` command over hand-editing `~/.claude.json`; that
  file holds a lot of other state.
- Optional working folder:
  `claude mcp add --scope user -e CLASSMCP_WORKDIR=/absolute/path classmcp -- classmcp serve`.
  If classmcp is already registered, run `claude mcp remove classmcp --scope user` first.
- Restart Claude Code, then run `/mcp` inside a session: classmcp should show
  as connected with 5 tools.
- If startup times out, set `MCP_TIMEOUT=60000` in the environment when
  launching `claude`, or use absolute paths.

## Host: any other agent

You are not Codex, OpenCode, or Claude Code. Before registering:

1. **Read your host's current MCP documentation** (fetch it if you have web
   access; otherwise ask the user for the link or the config file location).
   Find: the config file path for a user-wide (global) install, the key that
   holds servers (`mcpServers`, `mcp`, `servers`, `context_servers`, …), how a
   stdio/local server is declared, how environment variables are passed, and
   how to reload servers.
2. Translate this server definition into that format:
   - name: `classmcp`
   - transport: stdio / local / command
   - command: `classmcp`
   - args: `["serve"]`
   - env (optional): `CLASSMCP_WORKDIR=/absolute/path`
   - startup timeout: at least 30 seconds if configurable
3. Merge into the existing file. Keep other servers and comments.
4. Reload the host and run Step 7.

Starting points (verify against the host's docs; these are configuration
shapes, not all validated live for this release):

- Cursor: `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (project), key
  `mcpServers`:
  `{ "mcpServers": { "classmcp": { "command": "classmcp", "args": ["serve"] } } }`.
  Docs: https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp
- Antigravity: classmcp setup detects `~/.config/antigravity/mcp.json` with key
  `mcpServers` (same shape as Cursor). Confirm the path in Antigravity's
  MCP settings before editing.
- Any JSON host using `mcpServers`: same shape as Cursor; add
  `"env": { "CLASSMCP_WORKDIR": "/absolute/path" }` if needed.

If the host does not support local stdio MCP servers at all, tell the user;
classmcp has no remote/HTTP mode.

## Absolute paths

Use these when a host cannot find `classmcp` (GUI apps and some agents do not
inherit the shell PATH):

```bash
# macOS / Linux
command -v node                                   # absolute node path
echo "$(npm root -g)/gcrclassmcp/dist/cli.js"     # absolute script path
```

```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell)
(Get-Command node).Source
Join-Path (npm root -g) "gcrclassmcp\dist\cli.js"
```

Then use command = the node path, args = [script path, "serve"]. Example:
`["/home/me/.local/share/mise/installs/node/22.0.0/bin/node", "/home/me/.local/share/mise/installs/node/22.0.0/lib/node_modules/gcrclassmcp/dist/cli.js", "serve"]`.

On Windows, some hosts cannot spawn the `classmcp.cmd` shim directly; the
absolute `node.exe` + `cli.js` form avoids that. Use forward slashes or escaped
backslashes inside JSON.

Never use a path containing `_npx` or `.npm/_cacache`.

## Tools

All tools return JSON text plus `structuredContent`. Read `errors` (each with
`operation`) for partial failures; the rest of the result is still valid.
`truncated: true` means your `limit` cut the list. `scanTruncated: true` means
an internal scan budget stopped pagination, so older items may be missing.

| Tool | Purpose | Key inputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_overview` | Due, missing, new, or graded work across courses, or the course list. | `view`: `due` (default) \| `missing` \| `new` \| `grades` \| `courses`. `window` 1–30 days (default 7). `limit` 1–50 (default 20). `query` filter. `includeArchived` (default false). `detail`: `concise` \| `detailed`. |
| `get_assignment` | One assignment: prompt, grade, attachments, rubric, submission history. | `course` or `courseId`; `assignment` or `assignmentId`. `maxDescChars` 0–2000 (default 400). |
| `search` | Keyword search over assignments, materials, announcements. All words must match. | `query` (required). Optional `course`/`courseId`, `kinds` (`assignment`, `material`, `announcement`), `limit` 1–30 (default 10), `includeArchived`. |
| `download_files` | Save attachments of one item, or specific Drive files. | `course`/`courseId` plus one of `assignment`/`material`/`announcement` (or their ids), or `fileIds` (max 20). `destinationDir` inside allowed roots. `exportAs`: `pdf` \| `docx` \| `xlsx` \| `pptx`. |
| `submit_work` | Upload files to Drive, then try to attach and optionally turn in. Best effort. | `course`/`courseId`, `assignment`/`assignmentId`. `files` [{path, name?}] (max 10, 100 MB each), `fileIds` (max 10), `link` {url, title?}. `turnIn` (default false). `confirmTurnIn: "I confirm turn in"` required when `turnIn` is true. |

Names are fuzzy-matched; pass ids when a name is ambiguous. Use
`get_overview { view: "courses" }` to get course ids.

Example calls:

```json
{ "tool": "get_overview", "arguments": { "view": "due", "window": 7 } }
{ "tool": "get_overview", "arguments": { "view": "missing" } }
{ "tool": "search", "arguments": { "query": "photosynthesis lab", "kinds": ["assignment"] } }
{ "tool": "get_assignment", "arguments": { "course": "Physics", "assignment": "waves lab" } }
{ "tool": "download_files", "arguments": { "course": "Physics", "assignment": "waves lab", "exportAs": "pdf" } }
```

MCP resources (for hosts that support them):

- `classroom://courses/{courseId}`
- `classroom://courses/{courseId}/assignments/{assignmentId}`
- `classroom://courses/{courseId}/materials/{materialId}`
- `classroom://courses/{courseId}/announcements/{announcementId}`

### Submission limits (important, by design)

Google only lets the Cloud project that created a piece of coursework modify
its submissions. For teacher-created coursework, attach and turn-in calls from
the user's own project return `403 @ProjectPermissionDenied`. This is a Google
restriction, not a classmcp bug, and cannot be fixed by changing scopes or
credentials. `submit_work` still uploads files to Drive, attempts the action,
and returns `blocked: true` with an `assignmentLink`. Tell the user to open
that link and attach/turn in manually. Turn-in is never attempted after a
failed upload or attach. Quiz answers cannot be set, and there is no
unsubmit or remove-attachment tool.

## Files, folders, and configuration

| Item | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config dir | `~/.classmcp` (mode 0700) | Override with `CLASSMCP_CONFIG_DIR`. |
| OAuth client | `~/.classmcp/credentials.json` (0600) | Written by `classmcp setup`. |
| Tokens | OS keychain; fallback `~/.classmcp/tokens.json` (0600) | |
| Allowed file roots | `~/Downloads`, plus `CLASSMCP_WORKDIR` if set | All upload/download paths must resolve inside these. |
| Default download dir | `~/Downloads/classmcp` or `$CLASSMCP_WORKDIR/classmcp` | |

`CLASSMCP_WORKDIR` must be set in the MCP host's server environment config.
Setting it in your own shell or per tool call does nothing.

Downloads never overwrite and never follow symlinks; a name collision becomes
`name (1).ext`. Limits: 250 MB per file, 500 MB per call.

OAuth scopes requested: `classroom.courses.readonly`, `classroom.coursework.me`,
`classroom.courseworkmaterials.readonly`, `classroom.announcements.readonly`,
`classroom.student-submissions.me.readonly`, `classroom.topics.readonly`,
`drive.readonly`, `drive.file`.

## Troubleshooting

Always start with `classmcp doctor`.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classmcp: command not found` | Not installed globally, or npm's global bin is not on PATH. | `npm install --global gcrclassmcp@next`; check `npm prefix -g`; or use absolute paths. |
| doctor: `fail OAuth credentials not found` | Setup never ran or used another config dir. | Run `classmcp setup`. Check `CLASSMCP_CONFIG_DIR`. |
| doctor: `fail OAuth credentials invalid` | JSON is a Web/other client, not Desktop app. | Create an OAuth client of type **Desktop app**, download it, rerun setup. |
| doctor: `fail Google tokens not found` / token corrupt | Not authorized, or tokens removed. | Run `classmcp setup`. |
| doctor: `warn Token is missing scopes` | Authorized with an older version (before 0.3.0 lacked topics scope). | Run `classmcp setup` to re-authorize. |
| Browser shows "Access blocked: app has not completed verification" | App in Testing and the account is not a test user. | Add the account under OAuth consent screen → Test users. |
| Consent blocked by administrator | School Workspace policy blocks the app or API. | Use another account or ask the Workspace admin. |
| doctor: `fail Google API call failed` with "API has not been used / is disabled" | Classroom or Drive API not enabled in the project. | Enable both APIs in Cloud Console, wait a minute, retry. |
| Setup times out waiting for consent | 5-minute loopback timeout, or browser did not open. | Rerun setup; open the printed URL manually. |
| Host shows classmcp failed / timed out | Host cannot find `classmcp` on its PATH, or startup timeout too short. | Use absolute node + `dist/cli.js` paths; raise startup timeout (Codex `startup_timeout_sec`, OpenCode `timeout`, Claude Code `MCP_TIMEOUT`). |
| OpenCode ignores the entry | Used `mcpServers` instead of `mcp`, or stale `opencode.json` overriding. | Use `mcp` key, `type: "local"`, command array. Remove stale entries. |
| Tool call "unknown tool" in `execute` runtime | Dot notation. | `tools.classmcp["get_overview"]({...})`. |
| Path refused by `download_files`/`submit_work` | Path outside `~/Downloads` / `CLASSMCP_WORKDIR`. | Use a path inside an allowed root, or set `CLASSMCP_WORKDIR` in host env config and restart host. |
| `submit_work` returns `blocked: true` / 403 `@ProjectPermissionDenied` | Google project restriction (expected). | Open the returned `assignmentLink` and finish in Classroom. |
| Empty course list | Account has no courses, or wrong Google account authorized. | Confirm the account in Classroom web; rerun setup with the right account. |
| Results have `scanTruncated: true` | Internal pagination budget hit. | Narrow with `course`, `query`, or a smaller `window`. |
| Anything printed to stdout breaks the host | stdout is reserved for MCP JSON-RPC. | Do not wrap `classmcp serve` in scripts that print to stdout. Logs go to stderr. |

If you cannot resolve it, have the user open an issue at
https://github.com/khurrambhutto/classmcp/issues with the `classmcp doctor`
output (it contains no secrets) and the host name and version.

## Uninstall

```bash
npm uninstall --global gcrclassmcp
```

Then remove the `classmcp` entry from the host config, and delete
`~/.classmcp` if the user no longer needs the stored credentials. Tokens may
also be in the OS keychain under the service name `classmcp`.
